en.title: 5 Netflix Franchises That Deserve the LEGO Animated Special Treatment
en.summary: After the success of the new LEGO One Piece animated special, fans are wondering what other beloved Netflix shows could get the brick-built treatment. We've got the inside scoop on which series are prime candidates for a hilarious, family-friendly LEGO makeover.
en.body:
The brand-new **LEGO One Piece** animated special is here, offering a delightful, brick-built recap of the live-action series' first two seasons. It's a testament to the LEGO Group's knack for distilling complex narratives into accessible, fun, all-ages adventures that still honor the source material. This approach, proven successful with **LEGO Star Wars** and **LEGO Jurassic World**, isn't just for kids; it provides a humorous, visually inventive perspective for veteran fans and newcomers alike. With **LEGO One Piece** paving the way, the question on everyone's mind is: what Netflix original will be next to get the LEGO treatment?

## The Next Brick-Built Blockbusters

Netflix boasts a library brimming with globally recognized franchises that would translate beautifully into LEGO animated specials. First on our list is **Stranger Things**. As one of Netflix's biggest original IPs, it already has a robust merchandising presence, including LEGO sets. An animated special could serve as the perfect gateway for younger audiences, softening the show's darker edges while still capturing its adventurous spirit. Imagine a LEGO version of Eleven's solo Season 2 journey, or even a surprisingly thrilling, brick-tastic defeat of Vecna. It’s a franchise practically begging for this kind of playful reimagining.

Another prime candidate is **BoJack Horseman**. While seemingly an odd fit for LEGO's typically family-friendly fare, the show's underlying themes of redemption and self-discovery, coupled with its sharp wit, could lead to a surprisingly poignant and hilarious special. A LEGO **BoJack Horseman** could tackle its existential crises with the signature physical comedy and visual gags that LEGO excels at, offering a unique take on the washed-up sitcom star's journey.

## Fan Favorites Ready for Bricks

Beyond these, the possibilities are vast. **Harry Potter**, though already heavily integrated with LEGO through sets and games, could benefit from a dedicated animated special focusing on a specific, perhaps overlooked, storyline or character arc from the expansive wizarding world. Similarly, **The Witcher** could be reimagined with a touch of LEGO humor, perhaps focusing on Geralt's more absurd monster-hunting contracts or the hilarious mishaps of Jaskier. Finally, for fans of animated storytelling, a **The Umbrella Academy** LEGO special could brilliantly capture the dysfunctional family dynamics and time-travel shenanigans with a lighter, brick-built touch. These franchises, with their dedicated fanbases and rich lore, are ripe for the LEGO treatment, offering fresh perspectives and delightful new ways to engage with beloved stories.

## What's Next

While details on future LEGO animated specials from Netflix remain under wraps, the success of **LEGO One Piece** suggests this is a format with significant potential. Fans should keep an eye on official announcements from Netflix and The LEGO Group for any news regarding new adaptations of their favorite series.

content_raw: Picture Credit: Netflix There’s nothing quite like a LEGO take on a popular franchise. Take the brand-new LEGO One Piece animated special , which — at its best — manages to present a fun and unique recap on the first two seasons of the live-action adaptation of Eiichiro Oda’s manga of the same name.  But even beyond One Piece , LEGO can take even the most complex and dense franchise and boil down its lore and plot to an accessible, fun, and all-ages story with fun physical comedy that nevertheless respects and captures the source material. Just ask anyone who has played a LEGO video game based on a movie franchise, or seen one of the LEGO specials for franchises like Star Wars or Jurassic World . Of course, LEGO specials (much like the actual product) aren’t just for kids, but offer a humorous and visually inventive reinterpretation of established and successful franchises.  Now that One Piece got the LEGO treatment, it’s only a matter of time before we get another LEGO animated special on Netflix. With that in mind, here are our picks for the Netflix originals that would make for the best LEGO animated specials.  Stranger Things Picture: LEGO Stranger Things is one of the biggest shows Netflix has ever produced, and its biggest original franchise. We already got a Stranger Things stage play in the West End and Broadway, an animated spin-off, and even a mobile video game. What this franchise is missing, of course, is an official LEGO animated special.  There are Stranger Things LEGO sets, so the assets already exist! Now, an animated LEGO special would be the perfect way to introduce new audiences to the franchise, especially kids who weren’t around for the initial release of the show, toning down some of the darker and more violent moments, adding more humor, and summarizing the at times complicated plot.  Indeed, just picture all the hilariously weird ways LEGO could get around to teasing (but not actually showing) the messed-up deaths in the show — like Bob getting eaten alive! — or the inevitable LEGO-specific gags like Vecna dismembering his victims suddenly turning into minifigures just disassembling without any damage done to them. This is not just a way of introducing the show to new viewers, but even for hardcore fans, it’d be a way to revisit the popular series without having to get through the slower or more awkwardly paced stories. Quite the opposite, as a recap special, a LEGO Stranger Things animated special would definitely find a way to poke fun at the Season 2 episode where Eleven goes on her own solo adventure that was very weirdly placed and received at the time, but in a way that’s actually satisfying to watch. Who knows, maybe LEGO could even make the underwhelming defeat of Vecna actually thrilling and satisfying!  The Witcher Though there aren’t official sets for The Witcher , this is a vast fantasy universe that’s just begging to be LEGO-fi
